steps: Check your virtual environment is active. Its name usually shows at the start of the terminal line.
Install the missing package with 'pip install <package>', or install everything with 'pip install -r requirements.txt'.
Run 'python -m pip --version' to check pip belongs to the same Python you are running.
In VS Code, pick the right interpreter with Ctrl+Shift+P, then 'Python: Select Interpreter'.

symptom: Windows says "python is not recognized" as a command
steps: Check Python is installed by running 'py --version'.
If it is missing, install it from python.org and tick 'Add python.exe to PATH' during setup.
Close the terminal and open a new one so it picks up the change.
If typing python opens the Microsoft Store, turn off the python entries in Settings, then Apps, then Advanced app settings, then App execution aliases.

symptom: pip install fails with a permission denied error
steps: Create and activate a virtual environment, then install the package into it instead of the system Python.
If you cannot use a virtual environment, install just for your user with 'pip install --user <package>'.
Do not use 'sudo pip install', because it can break the Python your system relies on.

symptom: IndentationError or TabError when running a script
steps: Go to the line number shown in the error.
Make sure every line in that block uses 4 spaces, not a mix of tabs and spaces.
Set your editor to insert spaces when you press Tab (in VS Code, click 'Spaces' in the bottom bar).
Save the file and run the script again.

symptom: Code that works for my teammates gives me a SyntaxError
steps: Compare it with the version the project needs, which is usually written in the README.
Newer features, such as the match statement, do not work on older Python versions.
Install the right version and create a fresh virtual environment with it.
